history.summary: Gaudiya Vaishnava (ISKCON) centre of Hubli-Dharwad. Roots: a 1976 pendal program by Yasodhanandan Swami in Srila Prabhupada's time; the Hare Krishna Gift shop opened in 1993; the centre opened in April 2002 in a rented building at Lingarajnagar, Hubli, where the utsava deities of Krishna-Balarama, Gaura Nitai and Prabhupada were installed on Sri Ramanavami 2002 (deities carved in Vrindavan). In 2005-2006 the Karnataka government allotted ~8.5 acres at Rayapur, where a makeshift temple was built in 2006; Lakshmi Narasimha deities were installed in May 2015. A grand new temple complex in Vesara style (project cost ~Rs 50 crore) has been under construction since 2011-2013 groundwork; one content-creator video reports its inauguration on 22 June 2026 - treat as unverified pending official word. NOTE: the actual location is Rayapur on the Hubli-Dharwad bypass (Dharwad side), not Hubli city centre.

name: ISKCON Sri Krishna Balarama Temple, Hubli
town_description: Rayapur is a locality on the Hubballi-Dharwad bypass corridor between the twin cities. It hosts the ISKCON Hubli complex on government-allotted land near the BRTS route.

travel.road: On P B Road / Hubballi-Dharwad bypass; BRTS bus stop nearby
